title: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi’s remarks at the press conference with his Russian counterpart:
text:
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi’s remarks at the press conference with his Russian counterpart:"

"I welcome Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and his accompanying delegation. We are pleased to host him in Tehran once again."

"Today we had a very important and fruitful meeting. Iran-Russia relations are strategic, and after the implementation of the Strategic Partnership Agreement between the two presidents, our relations have taken on more important dimensions."

"Today we held detailed discussions on the most important regional and international issues, as well as issues of interest in our bilateral relations."

"In our bilateral relations, we examined practical solutions for expanding ties in the economic, commercial, political, and cultural fields. Fortunately, relations between the two countries are progressing well, and there is no serious obstacle to expanding them. We have continuous consultations with each other in the political sphere."

"We also have close cooperation on regional issues. Today we exchanged views on West Asia, the Persian Gulf, the Caucasus, Europe, Iran-US talks, Ukraine-related issues, and other matters."

"Our common view with Russia is that regional issues have no military solution; they must be pursued through diplomacy and political solutions."

"We also discussed Palestine, Lebanon, and Yemen. The genocide in Palestine and the dangerous expansionism of the Israeli regime must be stopped."

"The current insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz is the direct result of US and Israeli regime military aggression against Iran, and it continues in various forms."

"We have serious concerns about insecurity in the Caspian Sea, including attacks on Iranian and Russian ships. We share views on Afghanistan, reducing tensions between Kabul and Islamabad, and countering terrorist threats."

"We will continue our cooperation on international issues, where we largely share the view of countering America’s aggressive unilateralism."
